description.narrative: The development objective of the National Slum Upgrading Project for Indonesia is to improve access to urban infrastructure and services in targeted slums in Indonesia. The project has five components. The first component, institutional and policy development will support institutional strengthening and capacity building of central government agencies (e.g., BAPPENAS, MPWH)responsible for the management of KOTAKU and will include: (a) institutional analysis at the national level as well as for a sample of municipal governments to identify the nature of support needed to facilitate inter-agency coordination during program/project preparation, implementation and supervision stages; and (b) strategic national upstream policy level studies to facilitate the development of government policy to support the sustainability of slum upgrading and prevention efforts. The second component, integrated planning support and capacity building for Local Governments and Communities will finance the costs of experts and community facilitators throughout the project cycle to support capacity building (including training, workshops, and knowledge exchange events between cities as well as urban districts) of local governments and communities in 154 cities to design and implement slum improvements, including the development of Slum Improvement Action Plans (SIAPs) at the city level and Community Settlement Plans (CSPs) at the community level. The activities under this component will build the capacity of participating local governments to design and implement slum upgrading. The third component, urban infrastructure and services investment support. This component includes two sub-components as summarized below. i) improvement of primary and secondary infrastructure and site development as well as construction of connecting infrastructure as identified in Surat Perintah Pencairan Dana (SIAPs) in 50 selected cities, and ii) support for tertiary infrastructure upgrading in the project cohort of 154 cities based on a CDD approach. The fourth component, implementation support and technical assistance will provide technical support, advisory services and training for Project Management Units (PMUs) at national level, and for Project Implementation Units (PIUs) at national, provincial and city levels. The fifth component, contingency for disaster response due to a high risk of catastrophic natural disasters in Indonesia, this provisional component is made available to finance preparedness and rapid response measures to address disaster, emergency and/or catastrophic events, in accordance with the applicable emergency response operations manual.
To improve access to urban infrastructure and services in targeted slums in Indonesia and to reconstruct and strengthen public facilities and settlements in selected disaster-affected areas.

title.narrative: Indicator 2.2. Percentage of kelurahans which have Community Settlement Plans (CSPs) that have been consolidated with SIAPs

comment.narrative: <p>All kelurahans/urban wards have developed the CSPs that consolidated with SIAPs. The CSP and SIAP were consolidated in terms of slum areas; priority activities to alleviate slums; institutional arrangements between kelurahan and city level; and investment plan to integrate tertiary, secondary, and primary infrastructure</p>

<p>The project reported a 100% resolution rate that exceeded the end target of 90%. The MIS has recorded 200,942 entries as complaints, sought information, and offered suggestions for program improvement. </p>

<p>At project closing, the project successfully alleviated the slum area of 11,382 Ha in 2,507 urban wards and 154 cities, exceeding the original and revised targets of 7,800 Ha and 6,360 Ha, respectively. The target for alleviating slum areas has been achieved based on the minimum access of 80% of households to five basic infrastructures, as defined in the PAD. </p>

title.narrative: Indicator 3.2. Number of kelurahans that have completed 90% of tertiary infrastructure and services implemented in slum areas

comment.narrative: <p>2,507 kelurahans completed the tertiary infrastructure works with a total of 32,678 sub-projects, slightly exceeding the original target.</p>

title.narrative: Indicator 3.1. Number of cities which have completed 80% of primary and secondary infrastructure works and services connected to slum areas

comment.narrative: <p>Overall, 37 local governments participated, which is more than the revised target of 30 local governments because more local governments can accelerate planning and preparation including land provision, DED, readiness of communities, and budget allocation,  than it was anticipated during COVID-19 pandemic. The 37 local governments finished 55 primary/secondary infrastructure investment packages. </p>

title.narrative: Indicator 4.1. Percentage of local governments that have project monitoring structure and provide regular information on project implementation

comment.narrative: <p>The achievement was caused by intensive facilitation from the PMU as well as national and local consultant team to the participating local governments in 154 cities. Efforts were also made to ensure the institutionalization and sustainabiliy of the monitoring system. 84% of local governments had a project monitoring structure in place and consistently provided updates on project implementation, exceeded the target of 70%. The achievement is higher than the target because the information was seen as meeting the needs of the local government task force to monitor progress of slum alleviation </p>

title.narrative: People provided with improved infrastructure under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement has exceeded the end target. The largest contribution from the improved infrastructure comes from the local government budget (90%) and targeted funds for water and sanitation have also helped in achieving the targets.</p>
<p>Overall, the project reported 8.9 million direct beneficiaries, of which 4.4 million were women. </p>

title.narrative: Establishment of functional task forces for slum alleviation at local level (%Local Governments)

comment.narrative: <p>By the project's end, 93.5% were reported to be active and fully functional, surpassing the end target of 90%. The role of the task forces is to ensure collaboration and functioning between various levels of government across multiple sectoral agncies as well as within communities.</p>

title.narrative: Indicator 4.2. Percentage of kelurahans with completed annual financial audits

comment.narrative: <p>A financial audit of the Community Board of Trustees established at the kelurahan level is regularly conducted on an annual basis. 5,813 urban wards/kelurahans out of 6,143 have completed annual financial audits of BKM. </p>

title.narrative: Indicator 2.1 Percentage of local governments that have completed Slum Improvement Action Plans (SIAPs) which have been approved by Bupati/Walikota

comment.narrative:
<p>The end target has been exceeded. The formulation of SIAPs has been facilitated by city coordinators and local consultants. Achieving the target completion of SIAPs was critical for NSUP’s overall success, as these five-years strategic planning documents become key reference point for all slum interventions, irrespective of the source of financing. </p>
<p>A series of capacity-building activities was carried out to improve capacity of the local governments in formulating and implementing SIAPs.&nbp;The Mayors/Regents have approved the SIAPs to ensure that SIAP are utilized as an integrated plan for slum alleviation at the city level. </p>

title.narrative: Percentage of slum dwellers who are satisfied with the quality of urban infrastructure and services (of which women, of which bottom 40%, of which poor)

comment.narrative:
<p> </p>
<p>The first beneficiary satisfaction survey was conducted in 2019-2020 through face-to-face interviews with the 100 kelurahans considered safest from the COVID-19 pandemic and a telephone survey with 1,030 kelurahans. The survey method was adjuste in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The satisfaction level of beneficiaries from both methods was about the same; the overall satisfaction level was 90 percent. The second satisfaction survey was completed in December 2022. Referring to ESC Survey (Evaluation Phase II, 2022), 95.5% of beneficiaries expressed satisfaction. Within that, 95.4% of the Low-Income Community group were satisfied, and 95.7% of women reported satisfaction. </p>

title.narrative: Indicator 3.4. Percentage of infrastructure built that is fully functioning

comment.narrative:
<p>The functionality of the infrastructure built was measured by spot-check surveys by national consultants, local consultants, and community facilitators. The figure above shows the percentage of functionality of primary, secondary infrastructure, and tertiary ifrastructure. Referring to the latest spot-check survey in 2023, 98% of sub-projects are fully functioning, exceeding the original target of 70%. </p>
<p>???????</p>

title.narrative: Indicator 3.3. Percentage of good quality of infrastructure and services

comment.narrative: <p>The quality of infrastructure was measured following the completion of civil work, which was carried through cascading survey by community, facilitators, and consultants and recorded in the project MIS. The end target of 90% infrastructure investment has een exceeded as 98% of the infrastructure investment has good quality (42,884 out of 43,630 investments).</p>

title.narrative: Indicator 1.1. Establishment of functional task force for slum alleviation at national level

comment.narrative:
<p>The national-level task force for slum alleviation was established and operational; this task force utilized the existing Housing and Settlement Task Force (Pokja PKP) led by Bappenas (Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency). The task force consists of sectors related to slums: housing, settlement infrastructure, water supply, and sanitation. </p>
<p>The Steering Committee of the National Task Force has been assigned to lead the program in January 2017. The operational level of Task Force (Echelon II) has been in place since February 2018, and has led the day-to-day operation of the CCMU. </p>

title.narrative: Indicator 1.2. Establishment of slum inventory database/profiling

comment.narrative: <p>A slum profiling database was established in collaboration with the Central Statistics Agency (BPS) to provide updates on slum profiles at the national level based on a BPS annual survey and ranking of slums by measuring the severity of the deficiencies in living conditions.</p>

title.narrative: Indicator 5.3 Percentage of sanitation facilities have been built

comment.narrative: <p>Construction of seven packages of sanitation and solid waste facilities in permanent housing areas has been completed, out of the targeted seven packages, which means exceeding the target of 75%. </p>

title.narrative: Indicator 5.2 Percentage of water supply facilities has been built

comment.narrative: <p>Construction of seven packages of water supply facilities in permanent housing areas has been completed out of the targeted seven packages which consist of water reservoir, distribution line, and household connections. </p>

title.narrative: Indicator 5.4 Percentage of schools and higher education building rehabilitated or reconstructed to projects resilience standards

comment.narrative: <p>Rehabilitation/reconstruction of Tadulako University and basic education facilities in 58 schools was completed by March 31, 2022, as per the project’s resilience standard including 13 for kindergartens, and 25 for primary education, 19 for higher education, through nine activity packages. All of the targeted buildings were constructed to the project’s resilience standard, exceeding the target of 75 percent of nine activity packages.  </p>

title.narrative: Indicator 5.5 Percentage of health facilities and public service building rehabilitated to projects resilience standards

comment.narrative: <p>The four buildings were rehabilitated/reconstructed (PIP2B building, BPKP building, Undata Hospital, Anutapura Hospital) according to the project’s resilience standards through six activity packages, exceeding the target 75% of six activity packages.</p>

title.narrative: Indicator 5.1 Percentage of housing constructed to project resilience standards

comment.narrative:
<p>The housing constructed to project resilience standards has been exceeded the target. The number of housing constructed is 1679 exceeding the target of 1,600 houses in 12 permanent housing areas in Palu, Donggala, and Sigi. 100% of the 1679 houses are met the resilience standards which are using RISHA prefabricated instant housing.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>Total beneficiaries of CERC is 88,848 people and women is 44,416 people or 50%. </p>
